item.title: Attackers have been exploiting critical Zimbra flaw to steal emails (2 minute read)
item.description: Attackers are exploiting CVE-2026-73570 in Zimbra Collaboration Suite. A crafted email can trigger unauthenticated OS command execution when zimbra-snmp and SNMP notifications are enabled, and Microsoft observed web shells, reverse shells, privilege escalation, remote-access tools, email backups, and credential collection. Shadowserver found 274 compromised instances.

item.title: Fortinet warns of critical FortiMail flaw exploited in zero-day attacks (3 minute read)
item.description: Attackers are exploiting CVE-2026-104286 as a zero-day, a CVSS 9.8 path traversal and NULL byte flaw in the FortiMail management interface that lets unauthenticated HTTP requests write arbitrary files and execute code. FortiMail 7.2.0 through 8.0.1 is affected, and fixed builds 7.4.9, 7.6.7, and 8.0.2 are not yet available, so admins should disable IBE or restrict the management interface to trusted networks. Compromise indicators include an added /data/etc/ld.so.preload and /data/lib/liblog.so, plus an archive account named archive234 pointing to 79[.]141[.]169[.]187, and CISA gave federal agencies until October 4 to triage and mitigate.

item.title: Revenge of the SD-WAN: Exploring and Exploiting Yet Another Critical Cisco SD-WAN Vulnerability (CVE-2026-76504) (6 minute read)
item.description: A single unauthenticated POST to /%6a_security_check mints an admin session on Cisco SD-WAN vManage through CVE-2026-76504, a critical authentication bypass Cisco disclosed on September 30 as an exploited zero-day. Cisco's login module checked the raw request URI while WildFly matched the decoded path, so the encoded request skipped the password check and fell into a session-continuation branch that trusted hardcoded internal usernames like viptela-reserved-cloudops. With ~1,500 vManage instances internet-exposed per VulnCheck, defenders should follow Cisco's advisory and hunt serviceproxy-access.log and vmanage-server.log for encoded j_security_check paths and viptela-reserved- usernames.

item.title: Solving the Identity Crisis for AI Agents (7 minute read)
item.description: Uber faced two issues with agentic identity: its current identity model wasn't designed to account for agents acting on behalf of users, and provenance wasn't properly carried across different agents in a workflow. To address this, Uber implemented an identity system in which workflows begin by requesting a workload ID from SPIRE. That ID is then presented to a custom STS, which verifies in its agent registry that the requested agent is allowed to run on that workflow and returns a JWT with the relevant details to the workload. To simplify adoption, Uber built a standardized Agent-to-Agent client that provides an automatic, secure-by-default path.

item.title: What We Should Do Instead of Trusted Cyber Access Programs and Open Weight Restrictions (5 minute read)
item.description: It is pivotal to provide defenders with access to the most powerful, cyber-capable models, whether open-weight or frontier models. Instead of restricting access to these models, we should shift the paradigm to focus more on restricting attackers' access. Frontier labs should implement low-friction, cross-lab Know Your Customer (KYC) programs, do more to detect and block attackers, and publish time-to-detection-and-response metrics. Victims of AI cyberattacks should also be encouraged to share more detailed information about the attack and the attackers.

item.title: Bitget hacked via zero-day in third-party security products (3 minute read)
item.description: A zero-day in a third-party security product gave Bitget's attacker a foothold on August 31, 25 days before the $387.5 million theft. The attacker later planted a web shell and C2 on a second appliance and pivoted to the production wallet job server, where a custom withdrawal tool forged risk-control parameters and drained wallets in under three hours. The vendors remain unnamed, and the North Korea attribution comes only from Bitget's CEO, so the takeaway is to monitor security appliances like production hosts and enforce withdrawal risk checks outside the wallet host.

item.title: kunglao-agent (GitHub Repo)
item.description: kunglao-agent is a Claude Code plugin for autonomous reverse-engineering tasks.

item.title: Gemini 4 Argon: our next era of frontier intelligence (9 minute read)
item.description: Google is releasing Argon first to trusted cyber defenders through its Fairwind Program. The model can find, validate, and patch vulnerabilities, including a healthcare flaw exposing patient data. It scored 68% on CWE-bench v1 and found exposures across 20 programming languages. Google is testing safeguards against prompt injection, misuse, and unsafe agent actions before wider access.

item.title: Drop (GitHub Repo)
item.description: Drop allows users to create sandboxed environments that isolate programs and agents while attempting to preserve as much of the development environment (user, selected config files) as possible.

item.title: Disrupting a coordinated model-distillation campaign (5 minute read)
item.description: OpenAI detected an extraction campaign beginning July 1, with spikes on July 24–25 involving 16,000 requests from more than 4,000 users. Related activity affected over 15,000 users and was disrupted by July 28. Operators replayed encrypted reasoning and used cross-conversation prompts, with OpenAI linking a core cluster to Moonshot AI personnel, restricted accounts, closed replay paths, added output checks, and shared indicators with partners.

item.title: Google: AI Is Changing the Pace and Profile of Vulnerability Discovery (4 minute read)
item.description: Monthly vulnerability disclosures doubled in 2026, reaching over 10,000 by midyear. High-risk flaws rose 167%, and exploited vulnerabilities averaged 18 per month, up from 10.5 in 2025. AI-discovered bugs more often enable remote code execution (50% vs 26%) and skew toward medium and low risk. Researchers saw rapid weaponization of n-days, including a BeyondTrust flaw exploited within four days of disclosure. AI-related CVEs also climbed, with 2,076 tracked since early 2025, though zero-days against AI infrastructure remain unconfirmed.

item.title: MetaMask Security Incident Prompts Exit of Affected Ethereum Validators (1 minute read)
item.description: MetaMask is responding to an ongoing security incident affecting part of its infrastructure. The company is proactively exiting affected validators in its non-custodial staking operations, coordinating with clients and partners. Lido confirmed the exits are underway, with final validators expected to be exited by October 7, likely incurring foregone rewards and possible downtime penalties.

item.title: UK rail cops' £320K face-scanning spree nets zero matches (2 minute read)
item.description: British Transport Police ran a six-month live facial recognition trial at London rail stations, scanning over 500,000 faces.

item.title: China-Nexus Hackers Compromise 350 Systems Across Asia With New Antino Backdoor (4 minute read)
item.description: Antino, a new Rust-based Windows backdoor that runs C2 entirely through Microsoft Graph API calls to attacker-controlled Outlook and OneDrive, compromised roughly 350 endpoints across Asia in a China-nexus espionage campaign that Cisco Talos tracks as UAT-11587.

item.title: Signal completes rollout of secure chat backups across all platforms (1 minute read)
item.description: Signal 8.30 brought end-to-end encrypted on-device backups to iOS and desktop, completing the secure backups rollout across all platforms with a standardized format, though attackers have reportedly begun targeting the recovery keys.

item.title: Ransomware Attack on Financial Lender Triggers Customer Lawsuit Within 48 Hours (2 minute read)
item.description: The Gold Star Mortgage Financial Group is facing a lawsuit from customers after an alleged data breach by the BrainCipher ransomware group. The lawsuit alleges that the ransomware group stole more than 10k files from the mortgage lender, including full names, SSNs, residential addresses, and other contact information.

item.title: A Realistic Code Execution Exploit Chain in OpenBao and Vault (11 minute read)
item.description: ControlPlane chained four OpenBao flaws into an unauthenticated-to-RCE exploit that forges a SPIFFE provisioner certificate via an ACME URI SAN bypass, hijacks an admin role through case-insensitive ACL paths, and crosses namespaces to restore a malicious Raft snapshot. The final step executes any pre-existing binary whose SHA-256 the attacker can guess, even on read-only images and auto-unseal nodes, and Vault Community Edition remains unpatched after IBM declined a mutual disclosure agreement. Upgrade to OpenBao v2.6.3 or v2.7.0, or, as a stopgap, remove plugin_directory and enforce ACME EAB via BAO_DISABLE_PUBLIC_ACME.

item.title: New Spectre-v2 BTR Attack Leaks Linux Memory Despite Existing Defenses (4 minute read)
item.description: Researchers from VUSec and Scuola Superiore Sant'Anna disclosed Branch Target Reuse (BTR), a Spectre-v2 variant that reuses stale indirect branch prediction entries in JIT engines after code is freed and reallocated. Proof-of-concept exploits against the Linux cBPF JIT recover the root password hash in minutes on patched Intel systems with default protections. Mitigations are merged in the Linux kernel (CVE-2026-64507, CVE-2026-64508). Mozilla is prioritizing site isolation over IBPB-based fixes.

item.title: Stack Unwinding Can Lead to Leakless Code Execution (7 minute read)
item.description: This post describes a code execution technique in which an exploit abuses POSIX “cancellation points” to eventually execute code. This works by executing DWARF bytecode to mangle the .eh_frame_hdr data that is used when unwinding the stack. While this technique was discovered in the context of CTFs, it has applications outside of CTFs.

item.title: A GitHub token was stolen. Now what? (11 minute read)
item.description: Invictus traced a run of 2026 incidents to stolen classic GitHub PATs, typically lifted from developer endpoints by info-stealers and used to map every reachable repository through bursts of /repositories/{id}/readme API calls before cloning. In one case, a single token exposed 1,100+ potential secrets across 300+ repos, and validating and rotating them took 30+ people over a week. Since GitHub keeps Git clone events for only seven days and api.request events require Enterprise audit log streaming, responders should scope to the token's full reach wherever logs are missing, then migrate off classic PATs to fine-grained tokens, GitHub Apps, or OIDC.

item.title: Pwnd Blaster: Hacking your PC using your speaker without ever touching it (6 minute read)
item.description: The Creative Sound Blaster Katana V2X soundbar accepts unauthenticated Bluetooth connections and exposes its proprietary CTP control protocol over BLE. Firmware updates also use CTP and verify only a trivial SHA-256 checksum, allowing an attacker within ~15 meters to install custom firmware without pairing or physical access. The modified firmware adds a full USB keyboard HID descriptor and repurposes an existing diagnostic task to type commands after boot, turning the speaker into a remote BadUSB device. A proof-of-concept payload waits ~20 seconds for USB to initialize, then types echo pwned and presses Enter on the connected PC. Bluetooth stays enabled in sleep mode with no user-accessible toggle. Creative initially declined to classify this as a vulnerability.

item.title: OpenShell (GitHub Repo)
item.description: OpenShell is NVIDIA's sandboxed runtime for autonomous AI agents, enforcing per-agent policy on file access, syscalls, and network connections at the kernel level. Its standout feature is formal verification of policy changes, which flags risky new access, like credentialed calls to a new host, and holds it for human review. Agents never see real secrets, since credentials are injected only into requests bound for approved endpoints.

item.title: cgg (GitHub Repo)
item.description: cgg (Call Graph Generator) is a tool that generates Mermaid diagrams of call graphs directly from source code.

item.title: Reco (Product Launch)
item.description: Reco maps active software agents, their identities, permissions, data access, systems, sessions, API connections, tools, workflows, and employee applications. Teams can revoke excessive permissions, disable risky integrations, and enforce access policies.

item.title: GLM-5.3 and the Spread of Advanced Cyber Capabilities (5 minute read)
item.description: Anthropic posted a blog detailing the threat posed by GLM-5.3 as a cyber-capable, open-source model. Anthropic stated that GLM-5.3 performed comparably to Mythos Preview in ExploitBench, an internal binary exploitation benchmark, and a test of open-ended offensive cyber capabilities when paired with a human expert. Anthropic also reports that a deceptive prompt subverted GLM-5.3's guardrails 64% of the time, prefilling the model's thinking tokens subverted guardrails 92% of the time, and abliterated versions of the model do not contain these ls. guardrails.

item.title: Agencies Withheld Records Needed to Verify DOGE Data Safeguards (2 minute read)
item.description: During the Government Accountability Office (GAO)'s review of DOGE's access to sensitive data, six agencies could not or refused to provide sufficient records. The SEC and NOAA disputed the GAO's authority to conduct the investigation and refused to cooperate. The VA and SBA also did not provide records but didn't cite a reason for doing so. At the CFPB, access was granted to 19 systems, with one DOGE team member being able to view, modify, and delete information in the bureau's primary human resources system. At the Department of Education, one DOGE member received limited access to two federal student aid systems and an admin account on the department's network.

item.title: PixelLeak: How AI Agents Exposed Developer Screenshots from Leading Tech Companies (5 minute read)
item.description: Glow Labs found 13,000 internal screenshots posted to public GitHub repos by AI coding agents at 300+ orgs. Agents bypassed GitHub's CLI image limits by creating public repos or using gitshot, leaking billing screens, treasury consoles, and unreleased features. Most images lived in developers' personal accounts, evading org scanners. To prevent this, audit personal repositories and gists, restrict agent auto‑approval, and add runtime hooks to block pushes to public or non‑org repos.

item.title: Apple patches CoreGraphics zero-day already exploited in targeted attacks (2 minute read)
item.description: Apple patched CVE-2026-86950, an out-of-bounds write in CoreGraphics that allows arbitrary code execution via a crafted file.

item.title: Official MCP Python SDK Flaw Can Let Malicious Servers Steal OAuth Credentials (2 minute read)
item.description: A high-severity flaw in the official MCP Python SDK let malicious MCP servers redirect OAuth token requests to attacker-controlled endpoints. Affected 1.x (1.9.1–1.29.1) and 2.x (2.0.0–2.1.1) clients sent the client secret, authorization code, and PKCE proof key to the attacker, enabling full account takeover with the app's granted permissions. Fixes are in 1.30.0 and 2.2.0. ClientCredentialsOAuthProvider and PrivateKeyJWTOAuthProvider also require passing issuer= to pin the expected login service.

item.title: Automated AI Agent Used to Bread Cybersecurity Nonprofit DIVD (2 minute read)
item.description: The Dutch Institute for Vulnerability Defense (DIVD) reported that they suffered an AI-driven breach. The organization said that the breach was “loud and very, very messy” with the agent working autonomously and over explaining itself in comments, allowing the DIVD to easily reverse-engineer its attack. The threat actor exploited a vulnerability in a vulnerability in an undisclosed software that the organization stated was not Citrix NetScaler.

item.title: Pentagon Personnel Agency Data Breach Impacts 3 Million People (1 minute read)
item.description: The Defense Manpower Data Center exposed unencrypted personal data through a vulnerable file-sharing server. Unauthorized users accessed files between October 2025 and July 16, 2026. Records included Social Security numbers, names, birth dates, contact details, demographic data, and military specialties. The breach affects 2.76 million living people and 294,000 deceased individuals.

item.title: AI Agents Are Privileged Users; Who Is Auditing Their Access? (4 minute read)
item.description: Enterprises monitor human logins closely but often grant autonomous AI agents broad production access via long-lived service accounts and API tokens. These agents can initiate, approve, and execute high-value actions end-to-end, collapsing segregation of duties. The piece lays out six controls: isolate agent identities, scope permissions to the minimum needed, assign a business owner, log prompts and tool calls, run periodic access reviews, and build an out-of-band kill switch.

item.title: Attackers Abuse ChatGPT Custom GPTs to Deliver RAT via ClickFix (15 minute read)
item.description: Sponsored Google results led victims to "Plus 5.6," a Custom GPT on chatgpt.com that answered every prompt with a fake outage notice pointing to a Google Sites ClickFix lure, and Huntress tied at least 40 incidents to the campaign. The eight-stage chain sideloaded malicious DLLs through Canon-signed (later Stardock-signed) binaries, hid its loader inside a WAV file and a NuGet package. It then unpacked a full-featured RAT from a custom encrypted file system that located its C2 over DNS-over-HTTPS. The signed hosts change with each wave, so defenders should detect behaviors instead: PowerShell spawning msiexec on GUID-named MSIs in %TEMP%, signed apps running from fake %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs folders, and self-restoring Run key and scheduled task pairs, which require killing the process before removing persistence.

item.title: NeedyMantis: Unpacking a post-compromise malware family used in targeted operations (14 minute read)
item.description: NeedyMantis is a modular post-compromise malware family deployed since at least October 2025 by China-based actors, including Storm-3069 from the DAEMON Tools supply chain compromise, against telecoms, universities, intergovernmental organizations, and government contractors. It was sideloaded as fake DLLs alongside legitimate software like Poedit, curl, Vim, and TightVNC, then unpacked from custom XOR-encrypted archives through shellcode loaders into a stripped-down PE format, and communicated over WebSockets with RC4-encrypted traffic and loadable modules. Defenders should hunt for spoofed DLLs such as WinSparkle.dll or libcurl.dll in unusual ProgramData paths, the hard-coded "firefox/21.0" user agent, and connections to corp.tripswithengine[.]com.

item.title: FBI reportedly declares ‘cyber security incident' after hackers steal agents' personal data (4 minute read)
item.description: The FBI told staff that a hack of its FBIJobs.gov portal exposed agents' and applicants' names, addresses, job titles, Social Security numbers, and some medical records, including blood and urine samples and psychiatric reports. ShinyHunters says it exploited an Oracle PeopleSoft vulnerability and is not demanding money, but wants the bureau to correct an earlier report about its activities. The portal remains offline, and the bureau has not publicly confirmed whether the breach meets the legal threshold for a “major incident” requiring notification to Congress.

He previously served time for extorting over a dozen companies, earning €1.5–2.7 million, and was released in December while still facing civil suits.

item.title: CISA Says Attackers Are Exploiting Two Critical Citrix NetScaler Flaws Globally (2 minute read)
item.description: CISA added CVE-2026-88771 and CVE-2026-88772 to its KEV catalog after confirming global exploitation. Both have CVSS scores of 9.5. The flaws enable unauthenticated command execution, remote code execution, or denial of service. CVE-2026-88772 requires DTLS, which VPN virtual servers enable by default. Administrators should patch, inspect for compromise, isolate affected appliances, revoke access, rotate secrets, and investigate connected systems.

item.title: BOK Faces Scrutiny Over Cybersecurity After Staff Data Breach (2 minute read)
item.description: The Bank of Korea (BOK) is facing scrutiny over its cybersecurity program following a data breach earlier this year. The breach occurred in May and June after attackers accessed a GitHub system used by a contractor for an online training program. The exposed data included employees' names, email addresses, phone numbers, positions, duties, and passwords for 186 employees.

item.title: Elementor WordPress Flaw Lets Attackers Create Admin Accounts (2 minute read)
item.description: Security firm Patchstack warns users of the Elementor Website Builder plugin for WordPress about a new CSRF vulnerability that could allow unauthenticated attackers to create admin accounts. The vulnerability is a one-click attack that requires an authenticated admin to click a link that sends a malicious REST API request to create the account.

item.title: Containers Are No Longer a Security Boundary (6 minute read)
item.description: The traditional view of containers as a strong security and isolation mechanism is being eroded by the plethora of kernel vulnerabilities being uncovered. This article explains how a recent vulnerability in the AF_UNIX subsystem can be leveraged by attackers for container escapes. The authors recommend moving untrusted workloads to MicroVMs like Firecracker or Kata Containers for untrusted workloads.

item.title: From Exposure to Lockdown: How AWS Neutralizes Compromised IAM Credentials through Managed Policies (15 minute read)
item.description: AWS automatically attaches the AWSCompromisedKeyQuarantineV3 managed policy to an exposed IAM user within 10 seconds of a public GitHub push, with the CloudTrail AttachUserPolicy event misleadingly attributed to the victim's IAM user rather than to AWS automation. Each policy version tracked real-world attack evolution, with permissions added to block Lambda-based cryptomining, S3 data deletion for extortion, and Bedrock API abuse after Permiso's research exposed unauthorized InvokeModel calls. Security teams should alert on unexpected AttachUserPolicy events in CloudTrail, treat the quarantine event as confirmation of active key exposure rather than as resolution, and rotate all affected credentials before removing the policy.

item.title: PolinRider is A/B Testing its Way Past Your Detections (11 minute read)
item.description: DPRK's PolinRider malware spread through GitHub organizations by force-pushing rewritten commits from infected developers' machines, planting VS Code folderOpen tasks that run an obfuscated JavaScript payload disguised as fa-solid-400/500/900.woff2 and, since September 28, fa-solid-300.llf. OpenSourceMalware traced 853 force-pushes across three Binary-Mindz repos and found variants with different paths, obfuscators, and C2-reported build markers running in parallel, which it reads as deliberate A/B testing, while copied author dates and reused commit messages quietly reverted three cleanup attempts. Defenders should flag fake fonts by file content rather than name, scan every branch through bare clones, audit force-push activity logs, and enforce force-push blocking and signed commits on all branches.

OpenShell traces actions, applies policies, and supports NVIDIA, Arm, and Intel systems. Sentry verifies identity, inspects requests, protects data access, and can quarantine agents within milliseconds. Anthropic, Salesforce, SAP, Scale AI, and more than 100 organizations are integrating these controls.

It checks each agent's identity, task, target resource, and requested action in real time. Teams can start in observe mode, then switch to enforcement to block unauthorized actions, as the platform logs every agent action and the decisions made, with context.

item.title: Google to critical infra orgs: Our AI scanners won't be evil, promise (3 minute read)
item.description: Google and Wiz launched Scan for Good using Gemini 3.8 Flash Cyber and Red Agent with authorized scans targeting public websites, APIs, and applications, while human researchers validate findings and handle disclosure. Red Agent found a GitHub Actions injection flaw in Snowflake's connector, allowing command execution. Other cases exposed 8.8 million files, hospital systems, elderly residents' data, and railway administrator sessions.

item.title: House of Apple 2 on modern glibc (10 minute read)
item.description: This walkthrough breaks down House of Apple 2, a glibc FSOP technique that bypasses the vtable validation added in newer glibc. It points a FILE structure's vtable to legitimate wide-character stream code, which then dispatches to a second vtable that glibc does not range-check. Step by step in GDB, the author turns that unchecked indirect call into an arbitrary call, pivots the stack, and runs a ROP chain to a shell. The technique still works cleanly on glibc 2.43 (Ubuntu 26.04 and Fedora 44). Exact offsets and gadgets vary between builds, but the underlying control-flow trick remains the same.

item.title: Sender spoofing in Proton Mail via display-name homograph (3 minute read)
item.description: Proton Mail's web interface can show a forged sender that looks identical to a real one. The attacker sets a display name containing an address-shaped string like sundar@gmaiI[.]com where the capital I matches lowercase l in the default UI font. Messages from domains without DMARC arrive in the inbox with no authentication banner, even when SPF fails. A Reply-To header can route responses to an attacker's address without showing it unless the user expands headers, and the spoofed sender also appears unchanged in macOS desktop notifications, outside the app interface. The issue was reported in February 2025, confirmed and bounty-awarded in April 2025, and can still be reproduced as of September 2026.

item.title: Graphalgo campaign spreads to Terraform providers and Go Modules (5 minute read)
item.description: Graphalgo malware appeared in two Terraform providers and two Go modules. Trigger conditions hide execution until targeted inputs appear, and the payload reports host data through Slack, receives encrypted commands through Slack and an Arbitrum Sepolia contract, then runs Go or Node code. Aikido recommends removing affected packages, isolating exposed hosts, rotating credentials, reviewing deployments, and reimaging machines.

item.title: Placeholder third-party[.]com Referenced Across 1,700+ Repositories Now Serves Malicious Content (3 minute read)
item.description: Someone registered third-party[.]com, a non-IANA-reserved placeholder cited in 1,700+ GitHub repos, including AI agent skills and MCP docs, and it now serves a ClickFix PowerShell lure only to Windows visitors, while yoursite[.]com and your-domain[.]com push scams to macOS users that static scans miss.

item.title: GitLab Email Addresses Can Be Weaponized for Supply Chain Attacks (3 minute read)
item.description: GitLab incoming email addresses embed non-expiring tokens that act as the owner across accessible projects. A leaked address can create merge requests, submit patches, or push code to private projects after changing project identifiers, and can be used to bypass IP restrictions via email. Aikido recommended that organizations reduce their attack surfaces by preemptively rotating the access tokens in their GitLab email addresses and by scanning for these addresses in their development environments and repositories as if they were any other secrets.

item.title: PhantomRaven: An LLM-Generated Information Stealer Developed for Bug Bounty Hunting (6 minute read)
item.description: A bug bounty hunter built PhantomRaven, an LLM-generated JS info-stealer, and pushed it through typosquatted npm packages that used HTTP-URL dependencies to fetch payloads on install. It grabs OS/hostname/IP data, Git/npm credentials, and CI/CD env vars from GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, Jenkins, and CircleCI, then sends data via HTTP GET/POST. The operator used compromises to file bug bounty claims on HackerOne, Bugcrowd, Intigriti, YesWeHack, and HackenProof rather than selling logs. Npm 12+ now blocks preinstall scripts by default. Use --ignore-scripts and a private registry to block this vector.

item.title: Hacking AI Customer Service Agents (10 minute read)
item.description: At DEFCON 34, Intigriti researchers reported on various ways to abuse AI customer service agents. This article walks through different methods to abuse the agents to send phishing emails, invoke tool calls, and bypass MFA. It also demonstrates mechanisms to steal third-party OTPs and poison knowledge base articles to deceive victims.

item.title: CARBONATO: a botnet built around an AI agent (6 minute read)
item.description: CARBONATO worms through unauthenticated Docker daemons on port 2375 via privileged, host-mounted containers, then installs the stock open-source Hermes Agent and overwrites its SOUL.md persona so that Telegram-tasked LLM sessions run post-exploitation and loot AI API keys before SSH credentials. ThreatDown recovered the toolkit from the crew's own open registry, which doubles as the fleet's update server, and ties the operators to Costa Rica through voseo Spanish, UTC-6 build timestamps, and a +506 Telegram handle. Keep the Docker API off the network, hunt for a SOUL.md containing "GH0ST" rather than blocklisting the legitimate hermes-agent package, and inventory and rotate AI API keys like bank credentials.

item.title: Help your marketing team find its next channel (Sponsor)
item.description: ThreatSpike tried TLDR after Google and LinkedIn ads fell short. Its campaigns now generate $25K–$75K in new business pipeline each. If your company markets a cybersecurity product, share this case study with your marketing team.

item.title: Island (Product Launch)
item.description: Island runs an enterprise browser and SASE platform combining ZTNA, device posture checks, and inline DLP to block unapproved clipboard, download, and screen-capture actions.

item.title: Introducing the Pixi Audit Beta (4 minute read)
item.description: Pixi Audit, now in beta, scans Pixi lock files for vulnerable conda-forge and PyPI packages, and --fix bumps direct dependencies to the lowest compatible fixed version before re-running pixi update. Matching relies on Basilisk, prefix.dev's new conda-forge vulnerability database, which links repackaged conda-forge builds to their upstream PURL and CPE identities so existing OSV and NVD advisories apply. For CI, --severity high sets the failure threshold, with JSON and SARIF output, though it doesn't cover statically linked binaries yet.

item.title: ceasta (GitHub Repo)
item.description: ceasta is a single C++ tool that combines an IDA-style disassembler, a pseudocode decompiler, a function graph, and an x64dbg-style debugger for PE, ELF, and raw shellcode, with a full GUI on Windows and a CLI with a ptrace debugger on Linux. Its built-in MCP server (ceasta-cli mcp target.exe) lets Claude Code or Cursor decompile, rename, and diff builds. With --allow-debug, it can also set breakpoints and call functions in the running process. The decompiler is best-effort, with no types or structs yet.

item.title: Brief hijack makes Elsevier domains redirect to LAPSUS$ “Chapter II” page (2 minute read)
item.description: Elsevier.com, Evolve.elsevier.com, and Submit.elsevier.com redirected visitors to a LAPSUS$ “Chapter II” page for at least 78 minutes on September 21. Researchers suspect a DNS, CDN redirect rule, or management account change. Elsevier restored service and said its investigation found no compromise of core platforms, customer data, research content, or operational systems.

item.title: OpenAI agents ‘infiltrated Australian government website' (2 minute read)
item.description: An OpenAI agent gained unauthorized access to a Medicare statistics portal in June. It accessed public and non-public files, including aggregate health data and internal filenames. Australia was notified on September 10 through a generic disclosure mailbox. Officials later said agents also targeted two state-government sites.

item.title: Proactive Defense: Hardening Code Pipelines and CI/CD Infrastructure (17 minute read)
item.description: Mandiant published a five-pillar blueprint (endpoint, repositories, artifacts, CI/CD, and deployment) for hardening the SDLC, prompted by campaigns that poison GitHub Actions caches, extract OIDC tokens, and repoint mutable action tags to publish malicious packages that still carry valid provenance. Standout recommendations include a seven-day cooldown before new public package versions become installable, pinning images and actions to digests and commit hashes, ephemeral runners with egress limited to approved registries, and replacing PATs with GitHub Apps and hardware-backed SSH keys. It also addresses AI coding agents, advising teams to keep .env files out of model context and require human review of AI-generated code.

item.title: Accelerating delivery of CVE fixes with a new Kernel release strategy (3 minute read)
item.description: Canonical is replacing Ubuntu's 4-week regular and 2-week security kernel SRU cycles with overlapping 2-week cycles that ship a kernel every week.

item.title: Astrana Health Data Breach Impacts Private, Confidential Information (1 minute read)
item.description: Attackers spoofed Astrana Health's main phone number and impersonated staff to access company servers.

item.title: CISA: Ransomware gangs now exploiting critical TeamCity flaw (3 minute read)
item.description: CISA has flagged CVE-2026-63077, an unauthenticated RCE in JetBrains TeamCity On-Premises reachable through the agent polling protocol, as exploited in ransomware attacks.

item.title: Critical Bifrost AI Gateway Flaw Lets Attackers Run Commands Without Credentials (3 minute read)
item.description: Bifrost, an open-source AI gateway for 20+ LLM providers, ships with management auth disabled by default, so a single unauthenticated POST to /api/mcp/client can register a stdio MCP client and run arbitrary commands as the gateway user (CVE-2026-90898, CVSS 9.8). That exposes every stored provider API key. The official Docker image binds the management API to 0.0.0.0, and v2.0.0 only fixed a related plugin-loading flaw (CVE-2026-86242, CVSS 8.1). Upgrade to transports/v2.1.0 or set governance.auth_config.is_enabled to true, and treat any exposed unauthenticated instance as compromised by rotating virtual and provider API keys.

item.title: BigCommerce Data Stolen via Ribon Apps Hack (2 minute read)
item.description: Attackers used compromised Ribon API credentials from a Fastr system breach to access BigCommerce merchant customer data from September 13 to 17. Exposed records included names, email addresses, phone numbers, and postal addresses. BigCommerce revoked the credentials, uninstalled affected Ribon apps, and notified merchants.

item.title: GitHub App Private Keys: 474 Leaked Keys Exposed (11 minute read)
item.description: GitGuardian tested 4,802 leaked GitHub App private keys and found 474 that were still authenticated as 440 apps. Forty-four apps held organization-admin permissions. 207 could write repository content, and with the keys having no expiry, the leaked PEM files can remain usable for years. Cases included an Actions token app installed across roughly 300 organizations, BuildBuddy's internal app, Crusher.dev, and a CDC-related app.

item.title: The Tale of Two INC Ransom Notes (8 minute read)
item.description: An INC ransomware intrusion across 175+ endpoints started in early August with randomly named scheduled tasks launching an obfuscated PowerShell implant and RDP lateral movement. After 17 quiet days, AnyDesk delivered netscan.exe and a BYOVD EDR killer (hwau.exe loading the HwAudio driver), and Impacket's atexec.py deployed the payload. Huntress onboarded after the incident, so initial access is unknown, and the gap points to an access broker handing off to an affiliate, who followed the standard note with a DATALEAK_PRESS_RELEASE.txt listing stolen files and threatening to contact clients within 48 hours. Defenders should alert on randomly named scheduled tasks, unexpected RMM installs, and new or unsigned driver services, and limit privileged accounts to the systems they actually need.

item.title: Handle Redirect (17 minute read)
item.description: EDR products typically register callbacks on handle creation to monitor when processes call OpenProcess so they can strip access rights before a handle to a sensitive process like lsass is delivered. This article demonstrates a technique in which an attacker calls OpenProcess on a benign process (like notepad.exe) and then redirects the received handle to the sensitive process to evade EDR detection. To detect this attack vector, a security product running at the kernel level can periodically scan all process handle tables and compare ObjectPointerBits decoded EPROCESS against the process that owns the table.

item.title: Revoking the token didn't kill the backdoor (6 minute read)
item.description: GraphWorm, an implant tied to the China-nexus group Webworm, uses a real OneDrive account over Microsoft Graph as a dead drop, and its "upgrade" task swaps all five hardcoded OAuth credentials for a spare account in one command, so token revocation only pauses it. It also identifies victims by hashing MAC, CPU, and disk serials, so renaming or re-addressing a host won't shake the operator. Isolate the host or block the app ID in your own tenant at the same moment you revoke, then hunt sign-in logs for that app ID, unfamiliar tenants, and non-browser user agents hitting OneDrive.

item.description: Watch this on-demand security demo from AWS and SANS Institute to see how governance, risk, and compliance strategies can help address risk across identity, data, APIs, and agentic workflows. item.title: Firmware Reverse Engineering Skills (GitHub Repo)
item.description: A collection of five agent skills for firmware extraction, static analysis, Ghidra reverse engineering, emulation, and security reporting.

item.title: Outerlimit (Product Launch)
item.description: Outerlimit provides a decentralized authorization layer for autonomous software agents. It finds agents, monitors behavior, and enforces policies at execution time. The system restricts token use by scope, location, and conditions.

item.title: pktz (GitHub Repo)
item.description: pktz is an eBPF-powered network traffic monitor with per-process and per-connection reporting.

item.title: Anthropic and OpenAI Models Still Attempt Restricted Actions in Safety Tests (3 minute read)
item.description: Anthropic's Opus 5.5 escaped or tampered with its sandbox in 1.5% of unguarded tests. With package-registry credentials, it took harmful actions in roughly half of simulated exercises. OpenAI's GPT-6 Luna bypassed “access denied” controls in 42% of runs - Sol did so in 64%. OpenAI plans third-party reviews covering safeguards, capabilities, and misalignment incidents.

item.title: Microsoft disrupts AI-assisted platform that compromised 12,000 accounts (3 minute read)
item.description: EvilTokens, a Telegram-sold subscription service ($1,500 upfront, $500 monthly), abused Microsoft Entra device code authentication to compromise 12,000 accounts across 10,000 organizations before a Microsoft-led operation seized 50 websites and 150 domains, and the UK's Met Police arrested two men. Its AI chatbot analyzed 5,000 compromised emails at a time to identify who could approve payments, who they reported to, and which impersonation ruses would send funds to attacker accounts. Microsoft described it as a shift where criminals can make sense of a compromised inbox in minutes rather than days.

item.title: North Korea's Hangro Revisited (20 minute read)
item.description: Hangro, North Korea's SoftEther-derived VPN and mail client for officials abroad, added a July 2026 management certificate whose SAN lists hosts in Pyongyang and Khabarovsk plus an internal CGNAT address, while its older 2024 chain fails every signature check, including the root against itself. Its Chinese callback traces to six Shenyang assignments under a single 2008 Silibank registry contact, though silibank[.]com lapsed and was re-registered in 2023. The researcher describes the DPRK "return leg" as layered rather than a single pipe, with dead-drop pickup during Chinese office hours, 10 GB ETRN-enabled mail relays for bulk transfer, and Hangro for interactive sessions, though no actual traffic was observed.

item.title: Stolen passwords are exposing America's water providers to hackers (2 minute read)
item.description: SpyCloud found stolen credentials at 1,787 of 10,000 US water providers reviewed.

item.title: UK cops arrest 2 EvilTokens suspects, Microsoft seizes 50 phishing kit websites (2 minute read)
item.description: Microsoft and UK police disrupted EvilTokens, a Microsoft device-code phishing service.
